title: Microcapacity surfacing — idea journal
content:
Goal:
- Surface small pockets of underused/reservable GPU capacity to product teams and self-serve customers so they can run short bursts with predictable latency/cost without buying a full Dedicated pool.

Problem context / why this matters:
- Customers often want predictable low-latency for occasional bursts (e.g., live demos, nightly jobs, surge handling) but don't want to commit to a large reserved cluster.
- Hosted API currently hides capacity signals; you can request more capacity via support, but that's slow. Dedicated exists but is coarse (monthly commits).
- We can offer a middle-ground: "microcapacity" slots (small reserved slices, short-term reservations, or surfaced spot-like but predictable options).

Who cares / personas:
- Growth PM running marketing demos that must be sub-100ms p99 for a 2-minute demo window.
- Platform engineer at mid-market customer who wants predictable SLAs for a feature pilot (1–2 GPUs for 1–2 weeks).
- Internal demo/QA teams who need occasional high-fidelity runs without manual infra requests.

Proposed product ideas (brainstorm list):
1) Capacity vouchers: buy n-hours/minutes of reserved throughput at a discounted, fixed rate. Allocated to your org, expires after window.
2) Micro-reserved lanes: tiny Dedicated lane options (e.g., 0.1–1 GPU-equivalent) with short-term billing (hourly/day).
3) Surfaced spare capacity: console shows near-real-time "available micro-slots" that can be claimed for a short lease. If claimed, route traffic with soft SLOs.
4) Preemptible microcapacity: cheap, preemptible units with clear fallback routing to hosted models. Useful for batch jobs.
5) Burst API: POST /bursts with desired latency & duration, platform returns allocation token and routing hints. SDK integrates token handling.

Rough PRD outline (very rough):
- Objective: introduce a lightweight, low-friction way to reserve short-term inference capacity to improve predictability for bursts and pilots.
- Constraints: must not add heavy ops overhead. Should integrate with existing routing/fallback logic. Billing model clear and auditable.
- MVP scope (2-week spike -> 8-week build):
  * UI: console "Microcapacity" panel listing offer types and current available slots (alpha: static simulated supply).
  * API: /reserve-burst (org-scoped), returns allocation token and expiry.
  * Routing: simple policy that maps token to dedicated routing policy (TTL).
  * Billing: pro-rated hourly receipts, separate line item.
- Non-goals: full autoscaling of micropools, complex market mechanisms, enterprise legalized contracts.

User stories / acceptance tests:
- As a growth PM, I can reserve a 2-hour micro-slot with p95 < 150ms for my demo, get a token, and route demo traffic through it.
- As a platform engineer, I can programmatically request 4 hours of microcapacity for a canary rollout and see billing entries when it ends.
- As an SRE, I can observe microcapacity usage in the Console and set alerts for failed allocations.

Success metrics (initial):
- Time-to-first-reservation (goal < 5 minutes after first discover).
- Fraction of demo/pilot incidents prevented because microcapacity was used (qualitative).
- Revenue / utilization: target 10% of idle GPU minutes reclaimed in first quarter.
- Customer satisfaction: 4/5 for predictability in pilot users.

Operational considerations / implementation notes:
- Leverage existing routing: token -> route policy -> bind to light-weight container or pre-warmed instance.
- Cost modeling: need per-minute unit economics (including startup costs). Short bursts penalize cold-start unless we keep tiny warmers.
- Eviction & fallbacks: define clear fallback policies (stream to hosted API models, degrade quality, or queue). Provide hooks for automatic fallback in SDK.
- Security: tokens scoped to org; audit logs on reserve/release.
- Observability: surface per-token latency, cost, and TTL in Console.

Experiment design (spike ideas):
- Week 1: fake supply UI (simulate spare capacity) to test demand signal. Run internal signup campaign for demos.
- Week 2: implement token-based routing with static, pinned micro-node (no autoscale) to validate latency and billing flow.
- Week 3: collect telemetry, iterate pricing sensitivity (hourly vs minute).

Open questions / unknowns (notes to self):
- Pricing: per-GPU-minute or per-inference? How to incorporate KV/cache warmness cost?
- Granularity: do we expose fractional GPU units or discrete tiny machines?
- Risk: Will this cannibalize Dedicated revenue? Need segment gating (limit to small orgs/trials).
- Complexity: How many edge cases to handle for preemption? fallback determinism is important for product trust.
- Legal / compliance: short-term reservations still need audit trail for Private deployments — does KMS / HSM interaction change?

Quick API sketch (proto):
- POST /v1/micro-reservations {org_id, duration_minutes, desired_p95_ms, preferred_region} -> {reservation_token, expires_at, allocated_zone, unit_price}
- GET /v1/micro-reservations/{token} -> status, metrics, billing_summary
- POST /v1/micro-reservations/{token}/release -> success

Console sketches (notes):
- Panel: "Claim micro capacity" -> choose duration / region / latency tier -> button -> shows token + copy-to-SDK snippet.
- Activity feed: recent claims, reclaim events, preemptions, and billing lines.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run slido with sales/customers (ask: would you use a tiny reserved slot for demos?) — target market research with 8 accounts.
- [ ] Spike: implement token routing to a single pre-warmed node (eng-serving-runtime assist).
- [ ] Pricing experiment doc: hourly vs per-minute vs per-inv. Build simple calculator in Console.
- [ ] Add UX mock in Figma (ask DEX for 2 hours).

Notes to self (voice):
- Keep it simple at first: static supply, conservative pricing, gated rollout.
- Emphasize predictability not cheapest price — customers pay for SLA.
- Tie into Optimize suggestions: if a workload qualifies, Recommend microcapacity during high-criticality windows.

Slack shorthand reminders:
- ping @kai for routing prototype; @sam for billing schema; @dex-team for mockups.

End of scratch notes.

-- hannah
